newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips no longer sees improvement in H2.
newsitem.headline: Philips no longer sees improvement in H2.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Monday it no longer expected an improvement in operating income in the second half of 1996 as it had previously forecast.

"Based on preliminary information for the third quarter it is most unlikely, as mentioned in the outlook paragraph included in the second quarter's report, that there will be an 'improvement in income from operations in the second half of this year compared to the same period of 1995,'" it said in a 10-line statement.

Philips said it believed it would be necessary to accelerate planned actions for recovery and that further details would be included at the third quarter results announcement on October 24. A spokesman declined to amplify on the statement or give any indication as to what measures might be planned.

Philips in July announced it would cut some 6,000 jobs from its Sound and Vision unit over the next 18 months as part of a restructuring. It said then that outsourcing to lower cost countries would be a key part of restructuring.

The Philips spokesman declined to say when the decision to issue the profit warning had been taken but said the move had been made to give investors time to digest its implications before next week's results statement.
"It's quite clearly an early warning," he said. "We felt that we should not wait until next week." -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
